queue.title: HELLA Launches Commercial Vehicle Brake Pads
queue.text:
HELLA Aftermarket , the spare parts and workshop business of international automotive supplier FORVIA HELLA, is introducing brake pads for trucks, buses, and trailers companywide for the first time, expanding its range to include applications for commercial vehicles. The products are now available worldwide.


At Automechanika in Frankfurt, HELLA will present the commercial vehicle brake pads to the international trade audience for the first time (Hall 9, Stand A80).

“Under the strong HELLA brand, we are consistently expanding our brake portfolio. We are starting with brake pads for trucks, buses, and trailers and will gradually expand the range,” says Dr. Marcel Wiedmann, head of the global aftermarket business at FORVIA HELLA. “Building on our established brake offering for passenger cars, we are now transferring our expertise to the commercial vehicle sector, reaching additional customer groups and strengthening our position as a leading brake supplier in the independent aftermarket.”

[IMG:1]

Initial Portfolio and Market Coverage

HELLA is launching an initial portfolio of 58 references, covering a wide range of applications and model variants. This provides competitive market coverage for fleet operators, wholesalers, and independent workshops, with broad parts availability and a clearly structured product range.

Design, Testing, and Certification

The new program is designed for the high thermal and mechanical loads in heavy-duty applications. Each brake lining features matched friction materials to support braking performance, service life, and comfort in daily operation. Where necessary, linings are supplied with application-specific accessories.

[IMG:2]

All brake pads are tested and certified according to international safety and quality standards, including ECE R90.

Brand Positioning and Existing Brake Range

Since 2024, HELLA has offered brake products under its own brand name; previously, the brake business was part of a former joint venture. HELLA offers brake pads, brake discs, brake hydraulics, brake fluids and chemicals, as well as a comprehensive range of brake electronics for almost all common vehicle types.

The existing range of brake pads covers more than 90 percent of the European fleet of electric and hybrid vehicles. For brake discs, coverage is more than 85 percent. The new commercial vehicle brake pads complement the existing portfolio for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles.

queue.title: AUMOVIO Launches Distributed Brake System
queue.text:
AUMOVIO is unveiling its distributed brake system, the latest generation of its electrohydraulic brakes. The company said the system delivers greater performance in a compact design. A major Chinese vehicle manufacturer has placed the first order. AUMOVIO plans to start production at the end of 2027.


AUMOVIO Distributed Brake Combines Two Systems

The distributed brake combines an advanced one-box brake with an electronic stability control system. The system operates fully electronically from the brake pedal through the fallback level. It also uses modern electrical and electronic architectures. This approach allows engineers to design smaller and lighter actuators.

The system frees installation space for components such as larger high-voltage batteries. It also gives manufacturers more flexibility when placing actuators in the vehicle. AUMOVIO said the distributed brake delivers greater performance than previous one-box systems. This performance makes it suitable for demanding applications such as highly automated driving.

[IMG:1]

“The mobility of the future is automated, electric, and increasingly based on new vehicle architectures. This transformation will not happen overnight, but step by step. With our solutions ranging from electrohydraulic to fully dry braking systems, our customers can draw on a very broad product portfolio,” said Boris Mergell, head of the safety and motion business area at AUMOVIO. “The new distributed brake system expands this portfolio even further. It gives our customers even greater flexibility, efficiency, and powerful performance. With its first series order, our new system is taking an important step toward high-volume production.”

Intelligent Redundancy Keeps Both Actuators Active

Current one-box brake systems for highly automated driving contain two brake actuators. However, they use only one during normal operation. The second actuator serves as a fallback. By contrast, the distributed brake system keeps both brake actuators permanently active.

This design allows them to generate braking force together when required. Each braking system can function independently during a fallback. Manufacturers can therefore make distributed brake systems smaller, lighter and more energy-efficient than previous one-box systems.

[IMG:2]

AUMOVIO said it has increased braking performance by coordinating the actuators. The improvement applies during normal driving and emergency operation. Most other braking systems act on only two or three wheels in fallback mode. The distributed brake system continues to access all four wheels.

This capability supports highly automated driving, where safety during an electrical failure remains crucial. Distributed brake systems can support automated driving up to SAE Level 5.

Modern E/E Architectures Expand Vehicle Applications

AUMOVIO uses the electrical and electronic architecture of modern vehicles for the distributed brake system. This architecture includes multiple power supply points and redundant electrical networks. The architecture meets requirements for braking systems without a hydraulic fallback. These systems require a redundant system with its own electrical circuit.

[IMG:3]

The system transmits the driver’s braking commands electronically. It does not require a hydraulic fallback with a mechanical connection to the driver. Manufacturers can position almost all braking system components freely in the vehicle’s front section. The electronic brake pedal remains the exception.

This flexibility supports new vehicle concepts and improves the use of installation space. For example, manufacturers can install larger batteries to extend vehicle range. The distributed brake system works with many vehicle types. Fully electric and hybrid vehicles commonly use redundant electrical and electronic architectures. Many new combustion-engine vehicles also use these architectures.

[IMG:4]

Brake-by-Wire Supports E-Pedal Design

The distributed brake system lacks a mechanical-hydraulic connection between the brake pedal and braking system. This design provides additional benefits. For example, engineers can increase the air gap between the brake disc and brake caliper. The system builds fallback brake pressure electronically with greater precision and speed. This design reduces unwanted friction between the brake disc and brake caliper.

A single e-pedal braking system can also work across a wide range of vehicle architectures. Manufacturers currently use slightly different variants for left- or right-hand-drive vehicles and different powertrains. Instead, manufacturers can equip these vehicles with the same e-pedal braking solution.

This approach reduces the number of variants. It can also lower development, manufacturing and logistics costs for suppliers and vehicle manufacturers.

[IMG:5]

Distributed Brake Expands Braking Portfolio

AUMOVIO noted that it draws on 120 years of experience in vehicle safety. Its recent braking developments include electrohydraulic pressure providers in MK C 1 and MK C 2 one-box systems. The company has sold more than 15 million of these systems since their 2016 market launch.

AUMOVIO has incorporated this experience into a brake-by-wire application. The design combines hydraulic brakes with an electromechanical brake architecture. The system aims to provide higher performance while using resources more efficiently. These resources include energy, installation space and costs throughout development, manufacturing and service life.

queue.title: 为什么视觉内容和数字资产管理在售后市场比以往任何时候都更加重要
queue.text:
Long before streaming platforms, smartphones, and social media, audiences watched movies without a single spoken word. Silent films relied entirely on visuals to tell the story, and people followed along just fine. Visuals carried the message then, and they still do today.

In today’s automotive aftermarket, images remain one of the most important ways products are communicated. Whether customers are browsing an ecommerce site, searching a distributor catalog, or comparing products online, visuals often influence purchasing decisions before a single line of product data is read.

As digital commerce continues to grow, managing visual content has become just as important as creating it.

Managing More Content Than Ever

Manufacturers today manage far more than product images. They are responsible for videos, installation guides, lifestyle photography, logos, technical documents, 360 degree imagery, marketing materials, and more.

[IMG:1]

As product portfolios expand and content is needed across marketplaces, ecommerce platforms, and distribution partners, keeping those assets organized and accessible is becoming more difficult.

The challenge is no longer creating content. It’s managing it.

Companies are asking questions such as:


• How do we get the right assets to customers and partners without creating more work?

Without a clear process, teams can spend more time looking for assets than actually using them.

Keeping Content Consistent

One of the biggest challenges is maintaining consistency across channels.

An updated image may be available internally while an older version continues to appear on websites, distributor portals, catalogs, and marketing materials. The result can be inconsistent branding, outdated information, and confusion throughout the supply chain.

This is one reason companies are turning to centralized digital asset management systems that provide a single source of truth and make it easier to keep content current across multiple channels.

[IMG:2]

Digital Asset Management Solutions such as TecAlliance Pixey are helping companies address this challenge by giving them greater control over digital assets while reducing some of the manual work involved in keeping content current across teams and trading partners.

A single product image may need to be published in multiple sizes, formats, and resolutions depending on where it is being used.

[IMG:3]

Historically, teams have managed these variations manually, creating duplicate files and increasing the risk of errors. Today, systems can automatically generate different versions from a single master file, including resizing, format conversion, border application, and optimization.

Instead of maintaining dozens of versions of the same asset, teams can manage one source file and let the system handle many of the variations required for different channels.

As asset libraries grow, finding the right content becomes a challenge of its own.

Companies are relying more heavily on metadata to organize assets using product attributes, brands, vehicle applications, campaigns, and other business specific information. A well-structured metadata strategy can turn a digital asset library from simple storage into a searchable business resource.

[IMG:4]

For the aftermarket, where product relationships and application data can be complex, being able to find the right content is becoming just as important as storing it.

Managing and storing content is only part of the challenge. Manufacturers and suppliers also need to deliver that content to distributors, retailers, marketplaces, sales teams, marketers, and other partners, often in different formats and through different methods.

[IMG:5]

Digital asset management is therefore moving beyond storage and organization to include how content is shared and distributed throughout the supply chain.

Organizations using platforms such as Pixey can more effectively manage, distribute, and deliver the right content to the right people across the supply chain.

Visual content has always influenced how people understand products and make decisions. What’s changing is the scale and complexity of managing that content.

[IMG:6]

Across the aftermarket, companies are dealing with more products, more channels, more partners, and more digital content than ever before. Keeping assets synchronized, creating the right versions, making content easy to find, and getting it where it needs to go are becoming important parts of managing product information.

Ultimately, effective digital asset management is about making it easier to find the right content, keep it current, and get it where it needs to go, so businesses can spend less time managing content and more time using it.

queue.title: Litens Aftermarket’s Scott Howat on Being a Brand Champion
queue.text:
This episode of DriveTime features Scott Howat, director of sales and marketing, Litens Aftermarket N.A.


- Cloyes Chairman, President and CEO John Hanighen on Being the ‘Gold Standard’


Howat said the company’s engineering-driven approach is what differentiates its belt drive tensioners. With a history of innovation dating back to its founder’s invention of the first belt tensioner in 1979, Litens has developed an extensive portfolio of patented technologies. Unlike manufacturers focused primarily on individual components, Litens engineers complete belt drive systems, with the tensioner and pulley system playing a central role in their operation. Howat emphasized that this engineering expertise and problem-solving approach allow Litens to deliver innovative tensioning solutions to the aftermarket.

Howat outlined Litens ‘ strategy for integrating Dolz into its aftermarket portfolio, following its acquisition of the European water pump manufacturer about three years ago. Building on the approach used to establish the Litens brand in North America, the company is taking a phased approach to introducing Dolz to the market and building brand awareness. Howat, who oversees the company’s North American sales and marketing operations, said the strategy includes a marketing campaign launched this year, with plans to formally introduce the Dolz brand at AAPEX.

Litens’ ability to translate OE engineering expertise into aftermarket innovation begins with its extensive OE product knowledge and data, Howat explained. This expertise also enables the company to identify opportunities to improve upon existing OE designs.

[IMG:1]

As an example, Howat highlighted Litens’ newly patented Easy Button Latch technology, which simplifies tensioner installation by incorporating the locking mechanism directly into the component. The innovation eliminates installation challenges associated with conventional locking pins. It demonstrates how Litens leverages its engineering capabilities to develop aftermarket solutions that deliver practical benefits to technicians.

• How Litens’ engineering expertise and patented tensioner technologies differentiate its belt drive systems. (5:00)

• How Litens is integrating Dolz into its portfolio and building brand awareness in the North American aftermarket. (6:53)

• Litens leverages OE engineering expertise and data to develop innovative aftermarket solutions. (8:30)

• Litens’ patented Easy Button Latch technology simplifies tensioner installation for technicians. (9:36)

queue.title: Momentum USA 推出 77 个制动器零件号 - Brakeandfrontend.com
queue.text:
Momentum USA announced that it has introduced 77 new part numbers in August.


Those part numbers include:

36 new part numbers in the AmeriStar brake pad line, which cover 28.7 million vehicles in operation. These include late-model applications for the Ford Mustang, Jeep Cherokee, Dodge Durango, and high-volume Hyundai/Kia platforms.

8 new part numbers covering 8.8 million VIO in the AmeriPlatinum Ceramic line. This line now provides late-model coverage for cars like the Toyota Corolla/Prius, Ram 1500, Jeep Wagoneer, Hyundai Palisade and Kia Telluride.

14 new E-Marked R90 Euro Coated Rotor and fully coated rotor additions in the AmeriPro line. This release covers BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Land Rover, Volvo, Genesis and Mini models.

[IMG:1]

Seven new EPS Friction brake pad SKUs, extending high-performance stopping power to applications like Alfa Romeo, BMW 2/3/4 Series, Maserati, Porsche Cayenne and Jaguar F-Pace.

The AmeriPlatinum Plus Max Duty line adds key heavy-use applications, including the Ford Explorer / Police Interceptor Utility, Dodge Durango, and Ram ProMaster 1500/2500/3500 and ProMaster EV.

[IMG:2]

New numbers across AmeriPRO and VGX add coverage for electric and late-model crossover models like the Chevrolet Equinox EV, Nissan Leaf, and full-size SUVs like the Ford Expedition and Lincoln Navigator.

You can see further details on the new parts on the Momentum USA website.
